title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
abstract: Successful tool-use trajectories are not necessarily useful supervision. Even successful interactions may underrepresent multi-step dependencies or contain actions that are unjustified by the information visible to the agent at decision time. We identify two coupled requirements for effective trajectory supervision: compositional coverage, so that important observation-action dependencies are represented, and decision grounding, so that each supervised action is supported by the learner-visible interaction history. We introduce Trajectory2Gym, which constructs executable interactions around under-supported compositional structures and derives supervision only from grounded decisions in their realized executions. Structural-support selection allocates the resulting experience, while parent-normalized supervised fine-tuning preserves the semantic interaction as the unit of training weight. This reframes trajectory generation as the deliberate construction of learnable interaction experience, rather than the collection of successful trajectories. Across five Qwen3 scales, Trajectory2Gym improves Tau1, Tau2, and BFCL at every tested scale, increasing the equal-weight three-benchmark mean by 16.9-29.8 percentage points. The gains are strongest in stateful and multi-turn interaction, where later decisions depend on earlier observations and feedback. Our results suggest that scaling tool-use agents depends not only on collecting more successful trajectories, but on constructing interactions whose dependencies are represented and whose decisions are learnable from the agent's visible history.
title_ko: 결정 근거 기반 합성 상호작용으로 툴 사용 에이전트 SFT

title: DRIVE: Fine-tuning via Data Contribution- and Diversity-aware Weighting with Prior Regularization
comment: Published in NeurIPS 2026. 39 pages, including references and appendices
abstract: Single-stage fine-tuning is pervasive, yet catastrophic forgetting persists when the source pre-training data is inaccessible. Data weighting affords a natural lever to modulate sample influence. Yet existing weighting methods lack a principled mechanism to explicitly arbitrate knowledge retention against new-task adaptation, and provide no unified differentiable objective to accommodate auxiliary signals such as sample diversity and sample characteristics. This is because current schemes privilege one goal over the other, and no explicit gradient-compatible encoding exists for such signals. To address this, we propose DRIVE, a principled and efficient weight assignment framework. It derives per-sample weights via a unified differentiable objective where three coupled signals co-evolve: Shapley additivity splits contribution into anti-forgetting and adaptation components, which are reshaped by a covariance-based diversity term and stabilized by a sample-characteristic prior. Far from a mere combination, this yields an end-to-end gradient-based scheme balancing stability against plasticity. Theoretically, we prove that DRIVE enjoys superior stability-plasticity guarantees over existing weighting schemes and enhances parameter estimation robustness. Empirically, it attains superior overall performance, faster convergence, and stronger robustness. Code at https://github.com/luciabcd/DRIVE.
title_ko: 샘플 가중치로 파인튜닝 망각을 줄이는 DRIVE
tldr: DRIVE는 샘플별 기여도(망각 방지 vs 적응), 다양성, 사전 특성을 하나의 미분 가능한 목적함수로 묶어 샘플 가중치를 정해 파인튜닝의 안정성과 가소성을 균형 있게 맞춘다.

방법: Shapley 가법성으로 기여도를 망각방지·적응으로 나누고 공분산 다양성과 사전 정규화를 결합.

title: REACT: Representational Early Analysis and Control of Chain-of-Thought Trajectories
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) generation offers an opportunity to intervene before a reasoning model completes its answer. But does the point at which risk is easiest to detect also offer the most effective control? We study this question with REACT, a conditional activation intervention that learns a safety direction from paired safe and unsafe trajectories and applies it once to an early CoT hidden state. The model weights remain frozen, and all subsequent tokens are generated without further edits. To study timing, we train directions separately at each of the first five CoT positions and evaluate ungated edits with full post-edit regeneration. Across three distilled reasoning models and three generation seeds, the strongest gains concentrate in a two- to three-token early window; on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, the effect falls to approximately zero at the fourth and fifth tokens, even though later states can be more predictive of risk. This separates risk readability from effective control: intervention timing must be evaluated through its effect on subsequent generation. On the same 8B model, REACT raises the rate of fully safe CoT-answer outputs on StrongREJECT-273 from 29.06% to 82.05%, while keeping benign refusal and usefulness near baseline. An anonymized implementation is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/REACT_official2-333B.
title_ko: 추론 초기 한 토큰만 조작해 CoT 안전성을 높이는 스티어링
tldr: 추론 모델의 CoT 초반 2~3번째 토큰 위치에 안전 방향 벡터를 한 번만 더하면 이후 생성 전체의 안전성이 크게 오르며, 위험을 가장 잘 읽는 위치와 가장 잘 제어되는 위치는 다르다.
bullets: 문제: CoT 중 위험을 가장 잘 읽는 시점이 가장 잘 제어되는 시점인지 불명확하다.
방법: 안전/위험 쌍 궤적에서 안전 방향을 학습해 초기 CoT 은닉상태에 게이트로 한 번만 더한다.
결과: 8B에서 StrongREJECT-273 완전 안전 출력이 29.06%에서 82.05%로 올랐다.
결과: 효과는 t2 부근 2~3토큰 구간에 집중되고 t3·t4에서는 거의 0이다.
한계: 특정 증류 추론 모델·데이터셋·생성 설정에 한정된 결론이다.
why: 활성 기반 게이트와 스티어링 벡터로 부작용(과거부 증가) 없이 안전 행동을 교정하는 사례이자, 읽기 가능성과 제어 가능성이 다르다는 표현 수준의 통찰을 준다.

title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
abstract: On-policy self-distillation enables post-training foundation models without relying on stronger external teachers. However, existing approaches rely on ground-truth question-answer pairs, human-curated problem sets, or other supervised signals. In this work, we reformulate on-policy self-distillation as a self-training framework, driven by self-generated question-answer pairs and privileged reasoning demonstrations. We push supervision to the limit: guided solely by coarse, high-level topic descriptions, the model synthesizes its own curriculum of queries and privileged reasoning traces without access to any human-curated prompts or answers. We find that self-distillation on fully synthetic privileged information enables a model to improve across multiple domains while retaining its capabilities on domains it is not self-trained on. We demonstrate the generality of this framework across text and multimodal domains, achieving consistent self-improvement on standard language benchmarks and Visual Question Answering. Our findings demonstrate that foundation models possess rich latent capabilities that can be amplified without external task supervision or curated problem distributions.
title_ko: 주제어만으로 스스로 문제를 만들어 자기증류로 개선하는 LLM
tldr: 모델이 주제 설명만 받고 질문과 정답 힌트를 직접 생성·필터링한 뒤, 정답 힌트를 본 교사 역할의 자기 자신으로부터 온-폴리시 자기증류를 받아 외부 데이터 없이 성능을 높인다.
bullets: 문제: 자기증류도 사람이 만든 문제·정답 데이터에 의존한다.
방법: 주제만으로 질문·정답을 생성하고 자기일관성·합의 게이트로 거른다.

title: Interpretable sparse fine-tuning with TopKLoRA enables faithful circuit discovery
abstract: Fine-tuning on datasets of unknown origin can create a backdoor in the trained model when the data includes poisoned examples. Difficult to localise and remove, backdoors can persist through safety training. While parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods capture the full parameter changes introduced during training, they are not easily interpretable. We present the full method of TopKLoRA, extending the preliminary proposal of Masiak et al. (2025), an interpretable-by-design LoRA variant in which only the $k$ largest adapter latents are active at each token. Unlike SAEs, TopKLoRA is trained purely on downstream loss, where optimisation pressure incentivises learning functionally causal latents. We demonstrate this sparse LoRA adapter in a sleeper-agent backdoor case study where we create model organisms by fine-tuning gemma-2-2b, Qwen2.5-1.5B, and Qwen2.5-7B on a poisoned instruction-following dataset. For each organism, we identify and ablate a circuit that is both necessary and sufficient to implement the backdoor. Furthermore, our new fine-tuning method produces sparse circuits that are up to an order of magnitude smaller than a dense LoRA baseline, allowing surgical ablation of the malicious capability without sacrificing instruction-following performance. Finally, we propose a technique to construct model organisms with localised circuits using TopKLoRA latents and gradient-routing, which we use to validate the findings of our circuit search algorithm. We consider these findings as a step toward interpretable-by-design architectures that provide faithful units of analysis without compromising model performance. We share our code: https://github.com/interpretable-finetuning/TopKLoRA.
title_ko: TopKLoRA로 백도어 회로를 찾아 정밀하게 제거하기
tldr: 각 토큰에서 상위 k개 잠재변수만 켜지는 희소 LoRA(TopKLoRA)로 파인튜닝하면, 슬리퍼 에이전트 백도어를 작은 회로로 국소화해 성능 손실 없이 제거할 수 있다.
bullets: 문제: 오염된 데이터로 파인튜닝하면 백도어가 생기고 제거·위치 파악이 어렵다.
방법: 토큰당 상위 k개 잠재변수만 쓰는 TopKLoRA와 대조 기반 회로 탐색(CLCD)을 사용한다.
결과: 밀집 LoRA보다 최대 10배 작은 회로로, 보류 트리거 프롬프트의 99.9% 이상에서 백도어가 제거된다.
결과: 어댑터가 여러 층에 걸치면 지시 따르기 성능이 오염 전 모델에 가깝게 유지된다.
한계: 7B 이하 모델, 구문 태그 트리거, 트리거·대조쌍을 알아야 한다는 가정이 있다.
why: 좁은 파인튜닝이 만든 행동(백도어)을 어댑터 내부에서 국소화해 부작용 없이 제거하는 방법이라 표적 행동 교정과 안전성 보존 관점에서 참고할 만하다.

title: Probing and Steering for Safety-Relevant Behaviours in Large Language Models
comment: 20 pages, 26 figures, 11 tables. Code, data and interactive interface: this https URL
abstract: Activation probes are computed directions in a language model's residual stream, used both to detect safety-relevant behaviours and, by adding their direction back into the stream, to steer them. We explore how the main design choices behind such probes interact, within one pipeline, on one model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), and across three behaviours: deception, high-stakes awareness and sycophancy. The pipeline crosses two estimators (difference-of-means and logistic regression) with three token-pooling schemes (last, mean and learned attention), selects appropriate layers to detect or steer a behaviour, and evaluates every direction twice: as a detector of the behaviour, and as a steering vector to push outputs towards the behaviour. Prior work read together suggests a read/write dissociation, in which logistic regression reads (detects) best but difference-of-means directions write (steer) best. We find that it holds for deception and high-stakes but not for sycophancy, where the pattern reverses. The reversal appears to follow partially from the data rather than from the estimators. The best pooling technique and the layer choice depend on the behaviour and data, and the layer that steers best can sit well before the layer that detects best. The right steering metric to use between changing a model's perception and eliciting behaviour depends on the task - and the two can disagree outright. The exported probes and directions power an interactive interface through which a user can score and steer text directly.

title: Why Constrained Updates Still Forget: A Functional-Path Analysis of Continual SFT
abstract: Supervised fine-tuning adapts language models to specialized tasks but can disrupt previously acquired behavior. Existing approaches constrain parameters, gradients, or replay objectives, yet the connection between the protected object, the intervening trajectory, and retained outputs remains unclear. We develop a functional-path account that decomposes old-loss changes along realized updates into the controlled direction, gradient staleness, probe mismatch, and finite-step effects. The account yields a conditional refresh budget and identifies the restoring direction supplied by informative replay. Matched QLoRA interventions separate constraint granularity from placement before or after Adam: placement strongly affects retention across the studied code-label audits, whereas the granularity interaction depends on the endpoint. Checkpointed generation separates endpoint recovery from higher sampled-path accuracy, and matched replay schedules reveal loss exposure concealed by final scores. A sequential-task comparison extends this distinction to backward transfer: subspace regularization and projection improve average retention while trading off different old tasks; supervised replay protects both more consistently in this setting. Additional response interfaces distinguish content gains from exact-response retention. These findings connect update-level protection to task-wise behavior and motivate mitigation through explicit functional anchors, trajectory evaluation, and joint old/new auditing.
title_ko: 연속 SFT에서 제약된 업데이트도 망각하는 이유를 기능 경로로 분석

title: High-Value Training Data from Noisy, Diverse Sources
abstract: Training state-of-the-art models increasingly requires learning from large, heterogeneous datasets whose examples vary in quality, domain relevance, and source of supervision. Dataweighting---assigning different weights to training examples---offers a general way to control how such data influences training, but learning effective weights at scale remains challenging. We develop a scalable approach to learning dataweights: given a small, high-quality target dataset, we use metagradients through the training process to efficiently optimize training-example weights directly for performance on the target domain. To scale beyond a fixed dataset and model, we learn parametric weighting rules that generalize to new and streaming examples and transfer from smaller models to substantially larger ones. We study reward modeling as a prototypical application, where preference data may be noisy, adversarial, synthetic, or mismatched with the target domain. Learned dataweights improve held-out performance, automatically adapt reward models to specialized domains, and allow mixtures of human and synthetic supervision to outperform either source alone.

title: Towards Faithful Data Selection: Statistical Limits and Scalable Algorithms
abstract: What does it mean to have an optimal data selection algorithm? Optimality is conventionally framed as finding a subset that minimizes the population error of the classifier trained only on that subset. Our starting point in this work is first to show that this goal is information-theoretically impossible unless the data selection algorithm has access to a validation set order-wise larger than the training set. This impossibility result motivates shifting from unverifiable population risk minimization to a one-sided guarantee that we refer to as faithfulness: for any candidate subset, we provide an estimable proxy that upper-bounds the difference between training on the full training data and on only the subset. We model training with the Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm and bound the Kullback--Leibler divergence between subset-trained and full-data-trained parameter distributions by the trajectory-accumulated gradient discrepancy. Minimizing this discrepancy gives a principled way to select a subset. Even though the resulting problem is NP-hard, we propose a swap-based local search that decreases the bound at every accepted step. It can therefore refine the output of any selector without worsening its bound. Finally, we provide experimental results on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 showing that it matches existing data selection baselines. Implementation of our algorithm and the code for reproducing the results are available at: https://github.com/Mehdi-Inane/data_selection_swap.

title: Verbalizing Activation Differences with Natural Language Autoencoders
abstract: Activation verbalizers translate the internal representations of large language models into human-readable text. The recently proposed natural language autoencoders (NLAs) learn this by reconstructing activations through a natural language bottleneck. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond the setting they were trained for. Here, we study this question for NLAs along four closely related questions: (i) Do NLA verbalizations exhibit compositional structure with respect to their input? (ii) Do NLAs generalize to finetuned versions of the model they were trained for? (iii) Can NLAs recover finetuning objectives in model diffing? (iv) Can NLAs be specialized for model diffing? Across four models from three families, our experiments provide evidence supporting a largely positive answer to all four questions. Specifically, verbalizations of composed analogy activations mostly name the target while rarely mentioning the subtracted word, and an NLA can be reused on lightweight finetunes of its original model without retraining, with reconstruction quality degrading noticeably only for the largest model. Verbalizing activation differences between Taboo model organisms and their original models recovers the concealed secret word for most organisms, and reinforcement learning on activation differences further improves this recovery on held-out organisms. We also find that NLAs can recover the finetuning objective without the finetuned model generating any token, since the most informative token positions precede the user prompt. NLAs do not yet match state-of-the-art model diffing methods on the emergent misalignment detection task, but outperform a blackbox baseline. Our findings suggest that NLAs can meaningfully verbalize differences in activation space, rendering NLAs a promising direction for future work.

title: DIAL: Steerable Language Models with Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels
comment: This paper introduces DIAL, a framework for fine-grained, efficient, and scalable control of LLM instruction adherence
abstract: When a user says "Keep it short", how short should the LLM's response be? More generally, users and applications require different levels of instruction adherence, but prompting does not reliably provide fine-grained control over them. We therefore study "steerable language models" that provide fine-grained numerical control over the degree to which models follow general instructions specified in text. However, existing approaches do not jointly offer fine-grained control, efficiency, and scalability across diverse instructions. To address this gap, we introduce DIAL (Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels) to achieve all three properties. For fine-grained control, we perform classifier-free guidance (CFG) with a frozen LLM to provide training signals for on-policy distillation of instruction adherence at different levels. For efficiency, we design a lightweight steering adapter that uses a classifier over the LLM's hidden states to compute a closed-form steering edit. The classifier adaptively sets the steering magnitude at each token based on the target adherence level, while accounting for the geometry of the LLM's hidden states to preserve response coherence. For scalability, the classifier is text-conditioned, allowing a shared adapter to support new instructions without per-instruction fitting, and training requires only instruction and request text. Evaluation across multiple LLM families shows that DIAL achieves a competitive balance between concept expression and response fluency, with concept scores increasing monotonically across adherence levels. We introduce SteerIF, an instruction-only dataset of 98, 625 concept, persona, verifiable, and descriptive instructions. When trained on SteerIF, DIAL provides fine-grained control over personas and, when combined with prompting, improves verifiable instruction following.

title: Combating Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Domain Adaptation via Knowledge Recasting
abstract: Adapting language models to new domains during post-training risks degrading previously acquired capabilities, a phenomenon commonly known as catastrophic forgetting. Existing mitigation methods largely treat forgetting as a consequence of excessive model drift. They therefore constrain updates by preserving old outputs, replaying old data, or regularizing changes to parameters and representations so that the updated model remains close to its previous state. We take a different view: Rather than pulling the updated model back toward its old state, we translate the new domain into the model's pre-existing knowledge space, making unfamiliar knowledge learnable through familiar procedures. Therefore, we propose Skill Schema Transport (SST), a post-training framework that transports new knowledge into the model's existing skill space. SST abstracts each example type into a skill schema, preserving its essential operations, dependencies, and verification steps while removing domain-specific surface forms. By recasting new examples as instances of reusable procedures, SST turns knowledge update from trajectory memorization into procedural reuse. In continual domain adaptation settings, SST consistently reduces forgetting while improving generalization to related tasks. Across two 3B instruction-tuned backbones, SST improves average final performance on streamed domains by 2.53 to 5.75 points over sequential post-training. It also lowers max-drop forgetting in all evaluated settings, with the largest reduction from 42.41 to 7.10 points on the Qwen-3B MATH stream, while substantially recovering the OOD degradation induced by sequential updates.

title: Where Do LLMs Learn to Recommend AI?
comment: 18 pages, 4 figures. Companion paper to arXiv:2601.13749
abstract: Asked what to study, which career to pursue, or what product to build, large language models (LLMs) often recommend AI-related options. We ask where this tendency comes from by comparing models before and after fine-tuning and by varying how questions are asked. First, pretrained models already include explicit AI/ML terms in the recommendations of 27% of their responses, and their released instruction-tuned versions do so in 59%. Second, fine-tuning models ourselves shows that this rise is not inevitable: general instruction tuning leaves the rate unchanged, but removing the 7% of instruction examples that concern AI cuts it by 14 percentage points, below the level of the pretrained models it starts from. Data rewarding helpfulness raise it by 9 points, while data ranked by the preferences of diverse simulated users lower it by 9. Finally, with models held fixed, asking for the "best" option or for what to do "right now" raises the rate by 8 and 18 points, whereas telling the model it is an AI advisor adds 4. Overall, the tendency starts in pretraining, and what models learn afterward, together with how a question is phrased, decides how strongly it appears.

title: Uncensored Is Not Unbiased: Abliteration Removes Refusals but Not Script-Dependent Bias About Taiwan
comment: 33 pages, 3 figures, 18 tables. Code, data and an interactive project page: this https URL
abstract: "Abliterated" ("uncensored") builds of open-weight language models remove the activation direction that mediates refusal, and are popular partly on the assumption that a model that no longer refuses is also free of political censorship. We test this on two matched pairs of 2-bit models: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, each against a community abliteration. Each model judged 22 statement pairs (on the Republic of China (Taiwan), 1989 Tiananmen, control countries) in Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese (a character-level conversion) and English, and answered 27 open questions per script. Script mattered far more than abliteration: the original Bolt scored +0.58 on Index S (-1: People's Republic of China (PRC) position; +1: ROC position) in Traditional Chinese, +0.57 in English and +0.05 in Simplified Chinese, and affirmed "Taiwan is part of the PRC" with probability 0.91 in Simplified but 0.06 in Traditional characters; abliteration changed its scores by at most 0.06, mostly by raising "yes" on both sides. In Qwen, abliteration removed every refusal on 1989 and raised scores by 0.21 to 0.34, yet the abliterated Qwen still affirmed that Taiwan is part of the PRC in all three scripts. Naming the state the Republic of China (Taiwan) raised every model's score by 0.10 to 0.33 but left the script gap. Control pairs showed no script gap; each abliteration changed only its declared tensors. In 740,000 web documents, Simplified text on Taiwan contained PRC-framing terms 3.7 times as often as Traditional text. A script direction could not be steered away; a contrastive stance direction raised scores in every script, and its negation lowered them. A four-sentence system prompt raised the abliterated Qwen to +0.93 to +0.97. Keyword scoring rules failed the models closest to the ROC position mostly for attributing or denying the PRC claim. Uncensored is not unbiased.

title: TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking
abstract: Using an LLM to generate training data for another is among the most general ways to train one, and it remains common practice. Some frontier teams have closed that route for their own models: what comes back is an answer, or a short summary, without the detailed reasoning trace behind it. That is a little ironic: they were themselves built on distilling human knowledge, and distilling an open-source model is still entirely routine; the restriction applies to their own outputs alone. Recent work recovers the hidden reasoning by replaying encrypted blocks across models. It somehow works, but it breaks the providers' terms of service, so it is not something a product can be built on long-term. We built the alternative. We take the context and the teacher's answer as input, and generate the reasoning trace ourselves, in the style of the student's own model family. Training is two-stage, supervised and then adversarial: a generator learns to regenerate the family's own reasoning traces from their context and answer, and a critic learns how real a reasoning trace looks. Applied to a teacher's answer, the generator writes one in the family's style. An independent judge rates how likely traces are to be genuine on a scale from 0 to 1: ours average 0.68, real traces 0.66, and traces selected by the critic from four candidates 0.82. These are authenticity scores, not correctness rates. We test the idea on five benchmarks with everything else held fixed. On general tasks the five training corpora are about the same; on coding, the generated reasoning beats Fable 5's own thinking content. With the same 5,000 questions and the same teacher answers, HumanEval+ improves by 3.7 points and MBPP+ by 7.1 at the final checkpoint, and the MBPP+ lead holds at every checkpoint. We suspect that reasoning written in the student's family style is easier for it to learn from.

title: Answering in the User's Variety: Calibrated Accommodation Pairs for Post-Training
abstract: People adapt how they talk to the person in front of them. However, chat models tend to respond in Standard English regardless of the dialect used by the user. A uniform answer can hide whether training treats these users alike, and output audits cannot tell as well. We trace how each post-training stage, from supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to preference optimization (DPO) and reinforcement learning, changes a model's tendency to match the user, and read what each update prefers from two content-matched replies, one matching the user and one not. Across 10 open model lineages, post-training standardizes replies to every informal cue, yet after adjusting for how likely each reply already was, the DPO update still favours matching British and Australian spelling over AAE and Singlish on 10 lineages, and models still produce AAE features when asked. We then introduce calibrated accommodation pairs (CAP), preference data that reward matching users' dialect density while preserving Standard English for Standard-English users. On a fully open model, CAP raises convergence on features it was not trained on without a detectable increase in dialect for Standard-English users or a cost in instruction following. In contrast, one-sided pairs reach a similar gain only by overshooting the user and imposing dialect. Our findings show that uniform replies can hide selective updates and audits should read the update as well as the output. Code: https://github.com/kouzhizhuo/cap-accommodation.

title: Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) can succeed with surprisingly few training questions, motivating a view of questions as carriers of distributional knowledge transfer. How can we assess whether a newly generated question is valuable for distillation, and learn to generate better questions---without access to its correct answer? We introduce Ask-to-Distill (\method), a framework that treats synthetic questions as distribution elicitors and optimizes the teacher supervision they expose along student-generated trajectories. A student-initialized synthesizer is optimized using a distributional surrogate for question value, computed from a frozen student--teacher pair without reference answers, correctness rewards, or per-candidate student updates. The reward combines teacher--student disagreement with teacher probability mass on the student's candidate support, together with length and diversity controls. The generated questions are filtered and deduplicated into a prompt-only bank for standard OPD. Across mathematical reasoning, code generation, and agentic tasks, our method improves average performance and teacher-gap recovery over unoptimized student-generated prompts and KL-filtered real questions, while matching or exceeding real-bank OPD in the evaluated settings. Signal analyses further show that optimized questions can elicit denser supervision and more total signal from shorter student responses, supporting elicited distributional supervision as an objective for synthetic distillation data. Our code, data and models are publicly available at https://github.com/GasolSun36/Ask_to_Distill.

title: Is Refusal Direction Universal across Low-Resourced Languages?
abstract: Refusal directions have been shown to transfer cross-lingually with near-perfect effectiveness across safety-aligned languages (Wang et al., 2025), reportedly regardless of resource level. However, the only truly low-resourced language evaluated is Yoruba, which is strongly misaligned and shows limited transfer, leaving open how refusal directions behave for other low-resourced languages. We extend PolyRefuse to three additional low-resourced languages (Belarusian, Bashkir, and Tajik) and replicate the pipeline of (Wang et al., 2025) on Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct. We find that universality is graded rather than binary: directions from safety-aligned and partially-aligned languages transfer broadly, while those from strongly misaligned languages fail to reliably modulate refusal behavior on any target tested, including other misaligned languages, once ceiling effects are accounted for. Geometric alignment and behavioral transfer are further shown to be partially dissociated. These findings complicate the universality claim and suggest that users of the least-resourced, most strongly misaligned languages may face weaker safety guarantees.

title: Behavior Beyond Text: Evaluating Refusal Transfer Failure in LLM Agents
comment: Raj Saha and Ekagra Gupta contributed equally and share first authorship
abstract: While large language models are increasingly deployed as tool-calling agents, their safety evaluations still focus primarily on their ability to refuse harmful requests in text. We investigate whether the refusal behavior in text transfers to tool use. We construct a benchmark of 2,304 prompts across four domains, consisting of matched triplets that present the same harmful or benign request in text-only, standard tool-enabled, and adversarially framed tool-enabled settings. We then assess tool-call safety using 20 predefined forbidden actions. Testing five models of varying sizes and families, we find that requests refused in text frequently result in unsafe tool calls. Under standard tool-enabled prompting, this divergence occurs for 10-52 percent of harmful requests refused in chat. To mechanistically investigate this gap, we identify a refusal-associated direction in the residual stream of each of the five models. We find that in tool-enabled contexts, the activations along this direction decrease in four of five models. Furthermore, lower activation predicts unsafe tool calls across all five models (AUC 0.76-0.86). However, restoring the signal to the respective text-only value through activation patching only prevents a subset of unsafe calls, primarily by suppressing tool use rather than by producing safer calls. Steering along the refusal direction nearly eliminates unsafe calls only at strengths that also suppress benign tool use or degrade the output quality. Our findings indicate that the identified refusal direction contributes to whether a model acts, but only partially explains the refusal divergence. Therefore, evaluating the safety of tool-calling agents requires directly examining their actions along with their textual responses.

title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Realistic Scenarios Through Representation Engineering
comment: Project page: this https URL Code: this https URL
abstract: Reward hacking is a major problem in current production machine learning systems, resulting in costly and dangerous failures. Here we study how to monitor for and mitigate reward hacking in realistic settings, including tool calls and long contexts. We apply a dynamic intervention to steering directions obtained by three different methods: difference-in-means vectors from labeled rollouts, gradient optimization-based vectors, and vectors extracted when models reference an anti-reward-hacking model spec. This dynamic intervention perturbs model representations less than uniform steering vector addition to the residual stream, allowing for more precise edits. We find that we are able to cheaply and significantly reduce reward hacking without correspondingly significant costs to model coherence or capability, and that steering vectors originally extracted from coding environments also generalize to reducing reward hacking in other domains. Our results pave the way towards latent space monitoring and control over realistic production systems.

title: WRDO: Weighted Refusal Direction Optimization in Aligned Language Models
abstract: Aligned large language models are trained to comply with benign requests while refusing harmful ones. However, recent work shows that this refusal behavior is fragile and can often be disrupted by simple activation- or weight-space interventions. In particular, refusal has been shown to be largely mediated by a single residual-stream direction, typically computed as a difference-of-means vector between harmful and harmless prompts. However, this standard construction aggregates heterogeneous harmful prompts into one uniform average, potentially conflating distinct refusal-related phenomena. In this work, we study whether refusal interventions can be strengthened by learning how to combine prompt-specific refusal directions. We propose Weighted Refusal Direction Optimization (WRDO), a procedure that constructs a composite refusal direction from a bank of per-prompt directions using learned aggregation weights. This approach allows different harmful prompts to contribute unequally to the final intervention direction. We evaluate WRDO against prior single-direction methods on three open-weight language models using three guard judges and HarmBench as an external evaluator. We further measure the effect of the intervention on general model capability through standard utility benchmarks. Finally, we investigate a defense-oriented setting in which the same optimization machinery is used in reverse to restore refusal behavior in an abliterated model checkpoint. Our results show that weighted aggregation provides a more effective and flexible mechanism for manipulating refusal representations.

title: Harnessing Textual Refusal Directions for Multimodal Safety
abstract: Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) depends on unsafe multimodal data for post-training alignment or activation steering. However, such data is hard to collect, must be gathered anew for each modality, and its collection and distribution raise ethical and legal concerns. In this work, we relax this constraint and investigate whether textual refusal directions, extracted directly from the LLM backbone, generalize across modalities (i.e., image, video). Preliminary findings confirm this ability, though effectiveness is conditioned by layer selection, steering strength, and cross-modal alignment, with the latter causing safe multimodal inputs to be spuriously steered toward refusal. Building on this, we introduce Modality-Agnostic Refusal Steering (MARS), a lightweight training-free approach that injects multimodal safety without the need for multimodal safety data. MARS corrects modality misalignment via activation centering, adaptively scales steering strength within a geometrically defined trust region, and selects the optimal intervention layer, operating at the first generated token. Evaluated on five SOTA MLLMs across safety, utility, and video jailbreak, MARS achieves consistent safety gains while preserving utility up to over-refusal. MARS reveals that safety-relevant structure is shared across modalities and that textual refusal directions are a powerful and underexplored foundation for multimodal alignment.
title_ko: 텍스트 거부 방향으로 멀티모달 모델 안전성 높이기

title: Self-Distillation for Supervised Fine-Tuning
abstract: Supervised fine-tuning treats the expert demonstration or gold response as a one-hot target, suppressing valid alternative continuations that the model would otherwise assign probability to. We propose Gold-Conditioned Distillation (GCD), a method that turns expert demonstrations into model-native supervision. GCD uses one model as both teacher and student: the teacher conditions on a prompt containing the gold response in context, the student conditions on the original prompt as at inference, and the student is trained to minimize the forward KL divergence to the teacher's next-token distribution at each gold response token. This lets the model use its prior knowledge to teach itself the new task: correctness is anchored by the gold response, while the soft target preserves plausible alternatives. Across various training tasks on Qwen and Llama models, GCD improves new-task accuracy over SFT and generally reduces degradation on general benchmarks.

title: Safety Offset Learning: When Benign Fine-Tuning Misaligns LLMs
abstract: Safety risks from fine-tuning are commonly characterized by the harmfulness of the training data:harmful fine-tuning is considered dangerous, while benign fine-tuning is often assumed to preservealignment. We argue that this view misses a more fundamental factor-the behavioral transition inducedby supervision. Harmful fine-tuning and safety-degrading benign fine-tuning can both be understoodas learning the same refusal-to-compliance transition, but on different data distributions. We studywhether such a transition learned on benign inputs can generalize to harmful requests. We constructbenign examples that an aligned model initially tends to refuse and pair them with their originalharmless responses, creating a discrepancy between the model's initial refusal and the supervisedanswer. Fine-tuning on these examples increases harmful compliance, but only when two conditionshold together: the discrepancy is large enough, and it cannot be resolved through a narrow surface-levelshortcut. With the induced discrepancy matched, varying only whether it is localized changes harmfulcompliance by an order of magnitude; raising the discrepancy does not help while a shortcut remainsavailable, and removing the shortcut does not help while the discrepancy is small. Building on thisobservation, we introduce SAFEOFF, a dataset of benign instructions rewritten to raise the alignedmodel's refusal likelihood and paired with their original answers. Across three aligned LLMs and threesafety benchmarks, SAFEOFF substantially weakens safety alignment despite containing no explicitharmful supervision, suggesting that fine-tuning safety depends not only on what data a model sees, butalso on which behavioral boundary the supervision moves.

title: NADS: Navigator-Guided Data Selection for Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting in Fine-Tuning
abstract: Catastrophic forgetting is a central obstacle in single-stage fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) on a new task, especially when the original pretraining data are unavailable. Synthetic data offers a practical mitigation path, but candidate pools are often noisy and redundant, making effective selection essential. Existing methods often rely on indirect proxy signals whose alignment with actual training benefit can be limited, while utility--diversity selection over large candidate pools remains computationally demanding. To address these challenges, we propose NAvigator-guided Data Selection (NADS), a fine-tuning framework for LLMs. NADS first follows the target fine-tuning recipe without preservation regularization to obtain a navigator model, whose deviation from the pretrained model exposes recipe-induced capability drift. It then uses the predictive divergence between the navigator and the pretrained model to score forgetting-aware utility for each synthetic candidate, and constructs a constraint set through an efficient utility--diversity selection strategy. Finally, NADS fine-tunes on the new-task data while distilling pretrained behavior on the selected constraints to preserve general capabilities. Experiments show that NADS delivers a stronger balance between new-task performance and general capability preservation, while reducing utility--diversity selection overhead. Code at: https://github.com/zjh-vinky/NADS.

title: Defending Against Dormant Poisoning Attacks Across Language and Multimodal Agents
abstract: Recent work shows that attackers can implant dormant malicious behaviors that remain hidden at release but emerge after benign fine-tuning. As foundation models are used as agents, whether dormant poisoning extends to harmful agent actions and multimodal settings remains unclear. We show two agentic risks: (1) harmful behaviors activated by benign fine-tuning can extend to unseen actions; (2) multiple harmful behaviors can coexist and be jointly activated by benign downstream fine-tuning. Existing defenses often rely on external safe responses, which are hard to obtain for agent actions, or a trusted clean reference model. We exploit a key property of dormant poisoning: the attacker must preserve safe behavior at release to conceal poisoning, and this behavior can serve as a safety reference. Leveraging this property, we automatically construct a Safety Buffer pairing harmful inputs with the released model's responses and benign versions generated by the same model to remove harmful intent. The Safety Buffer can replace external safe responses in existing defenses, but these defenses do not distinguish updates that weaken safety from those that preserve it, often increasing over-refusal or reducing utility. To address this limitation, we introduce LookAhead Defense, which previews benign fine-tuning updates using the Safety Buffer and penalizes only updates predicted to weaken safe behavior on harmful inputs or increase the likelihood of refusals on benign versions in the Safety Buffer. Across language models, language agents, and multimodal agents, LookAhead Defense reduces harmful behavior in agents from up to 93.9% to at most 14.2% and harmful responses in language models from up to 92.5% to at most 2.0% versus vanilla fine-tuning, while maintaining competitive utility and low over-refusal. It remains effective against other poisoning methods.

title: Policy Is Not Capability: Some Safety Benchmarks Measure Which Definition of "Unsafe" You Trained On
comment: Accepted as a poster at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop TAE (Trust-AI-Eval): Can We Trust AI Evaluation?, Sydney. 20 pages, 5 figures
abstract: A guardrail classifier is reported as if unsafe were a property of text. It is not: it is a property of a policy, and the policy enters the model through its labels. We exploit an accident of an industrial deployment in which the same ~53k prompts were labelled twice, under two operational definitions ("is this a request for harmful content?" and "would a moderator block this?"), and used to train ten guardrail arms sharing architecture, codebase and optimiser family, at two model scales. First, the guardrail's own training corpus already contained the benchmarks: JailbreakBench-benign is 88% and OR-Bench-hard 82% present in the training pools, two over-refusal benchmarks, the kind a guardrail reports to argue it does not over-block. Everything below is decontaminated. Second, safety benchmarks stratify sharply by how much of their score is decided by the label definition rather than by the model: with architecture and optimiser fixed, the range across the ten arms is 0.99 on HarmBench-copyright and 0.043 on WildGuard-benign, a 23x spread. Third, a benchmark score can be moved across its entire range by 0.03% of the parameters. Across these arms HarmBench-copyright spans 0-100 and OR-Bench-hard over-refusal 3.4-56.4%, and the four arms whose last supervision signal carries a given policy occupy one extreme of both (exact rank p=0.005, or 0.04-0.14 at worst), at unchanged detection capability. For a distilled student the teacher's soft labels do this even when every hard label carries the other policy, so teacher provenance is an unrecorded confound in any released checkpoint. Fourth, validation accuracy on the one split that grades all twenty arms tracks agreement with the annotator's policy (rho=+0.74), not detection capability (rho=+0.34). We argue that guardrail evaluations should report contamination, a seed floor and the definition they were graded against as first-class variables.

title: From Stories to Features: Scaling Concept Vectors for AI Alignment & Interpretability
comment: 51 pages, 41 figures, 26 tables. Code: this https URL
abstract: We study feature vectors: directions in a language model's activation space that correspond to human-interpretable concepts, such as honesty or deception. Existing unsupervised methods like sparse autoencoders attempt to recover the whole feature space, often at the cost of feature quality and interpretability. We take a more pragmatic route: focusing on concepts relevant to AI safety and alignment, we generate synthetic concept-antagonist story pairs and use the difference of their mean model activations as a feature vector. We scale this approach to 1,036 alignment-relevant concepts using 2M synthetic stories across multiple languages and genres, which we publicly release. Across six models from three model families, our feature vectors reliably generalize to detecting their corresponding concepts in chat dialogues and web text. They form an interpretable geometry shared across models and can causally steer model behavior when injected into activations. We further use these features to analyze model representations during jailbreak attacks, mathematical and agentic reasoning. Our targeted feature construction thus offers a scalable route to studying concepts in language models, potentially extending to millions of features across arbitrary domains.

title: Compositional Activation Steering Across Languages and Behaviors with Contextual Gates
abstract: Activation steering has emerged as an effective and precise way to influence the behaviours of language models. However, composing multiple steering directions to control several behaviours simultaneously remains challenging, particularly in multilingual settings and with training-free steering vectors. We address this challenge with contextual steering, jointly training gates that adapt the strength of fixed steering directions to the current hidden state and interactions between interventions. Across a broad range of languages, behavioural attributes, and models, our approach outperforms constant-strength steering and four strong baselines, including prompting. It also better preserves general knowledge and keeps the model's internal computation closer to that of the prompted model. Our analysis further shows how jointly trained gates adapt their contributions during composition, explaining the mechanisms underlying effective compositional steering.
title_ko: 문맥 의존 게이트로 언어·행동 조향 벡터를 함께 합성하는 방법
tldr: 고정된 조향 방향의 세기를 은닉 상태에 따라 정하는 게이트를 여러 속성에 대해 함께 학습해, 언어와 행동 속성을 동시에 더 잘 제어하고 일반 지식도 더 잘 보존한다.
bullets: 문제: 여러 조향 벡터를 합치면 서로 간섭하고, 고정 세기는 문맥에 못 맞춘다.
방법: 방향은 고정하고 층별 아핀 게이트가 세기를 정하며, 여러 속성은 공동 학습한다.
결과: 9개 모델·9개 언어·14개 행동에서 고정 세기 조향과 프롬프팅 등 4개 기준선을 앞섰다고 보고한다.
결과: 일반 지식 보존이 더 낫고 내부 계산이 프롬프트 모델에 더 가깝다.

title: DeGMatch: Target-Aware Reasoning Data Selection via Deconfounded Gradient Matching
abstract: Reasoning post-training on long trajectories has substantially improved the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but scaling such training to large datasets is increasingly expensive. We study target-aware reasoning data selection, where a small reference set specifies a target capability and guides the selection of training trajectories for specialization. We find that existing target-aware methods can exhibit limited target discrimination on long reasoning trajectories, while dominant population-level structure in candidate gradients can obscure finer target-dependent variation during gradient matching. To address these limitations, we introduce Deconfounded Gradient Matching (DeGMatch), which first constructs a target-relevance gate and then reranks candidates using model-specific gradients. DeGMatch centers gradients using the candidate-population mean and removes leading principal directions before target matching, reducing the influence of dominant population-level structure and improving target discrimination. Across mathematics, science, and code, DeGMatch outperforms strong heuristic, target-aware, and reasoning-specific data selection baselines, while remaining effective across selection budgets, model families, and scales. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/CHLee0801/degmatch.
title_ko: 공통 그래디언트 구조를 제거해 추론 데이터를 목표별로 선별
tldr: 추론 궤적의 그래디언트에서 후보 전체가 공유하는 지배적 방향(평균과 상위 주성분)을 제거한 뒤 소량의 참조 세트와 매칭하면, 목표 능력에 맞는 학습 데이터를 더 잘 고를 수 있다.
bullets: 문제: 긴 추론 궤적에서는 기존 목표 인식 선별이 목표를 잘 구분하지 못한다.
방법: 관련성 게이트로 후보를 좁히고, 평균·상위 PC를 뺀 그래디언트로 재순위한다.

title: Hidden Cartographer: Hidden State Guided Data Selection for Dual Budgeted Instruction Tuning
abstract: Given the high cost of expert annotation and limited fine-tuning resources, effective data selection from large unlabeled pools under strict budgets has become a crucial step in adapting LLMs to specialized domains. Existing label-dependent methods risk distorted selection when using pseudo-labels, while traditional active learning methods do not explicitly characterize instruction-tuning dynamics. To address these limitations, we propose Hidden Cartographer (HC), a two-stage framework that uses hidden states to guide annotation and exact training dynamics to select the final training subset. The first stage is Progressive Candidate Expansion, which utilizes the proxy to iteratively select top unlabeled candidates for expert annotation, merging them to recompute training dynamics and update the proxy until the annotation budget is exhausted; the second stage is Exact Cartography Pruning, which ranks these annotated candidates by their exact dynamics scores to isolate a compact subset under the final training budget. Experiments across the medical, legal, and financial domains demonstrate that HC achieves the highest average accuracy among all budgeted baselines, requiring annotation for only 20--30% of the original pool and fine-tuning on just 10--15%.
title_ko: 은닉 상태로 주석·학습 예산을 모두 줄이는 데이터 선택

bullets: 문제: 전문가 주석 비용과 학습 자원이 모두 제한된 상황에서 라벨 없는 풀의 데이터 선택이 어렵다.
방법: 은닉 상태 프록시로 후보를 점진 확장해 주석하고, 정확한 동역학 점수로 가지치기한다.

title: Safety Mid-Training: Internalizing LLM Safety as a Foundational Capability
abstract: Safety alignment for large language models (LLMs) is primarily performed during post-training, while recent work has also begun incorporating safety data into pre-training. Yet safety can degrade when later training no longer includes safety data, and gains in safety often come at the cost of general capability. This tension suggests that safety and general reasoning should not be treated as separate training goals. We instead view safety as an LLM capability that can be learned through a reasoning structure shared with general tasks. Both require the model to understand intent or task goals, apply relevant knowledge, and reason about potential consequences. We introduce safety mid-training, a stage between pre-training and post-training that jointly develops safety and general reasoning through this shared structure. Given safety and utility prompts, the base model generates structured documents and reasoning traces that are then used for mid-training. Safety mid-training reduces average attack success rate (ASR) by 72% to 81% relative to Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B base models, while also improving general capability. The benefits persist through subsequent post-training. After general-only SFT, mid-trained models largely retain their safety, achieving lower ASR than the baselines without sacrificing general capability. They also retain safety under general-only GRPO without safety rewards, while subsequent RL reaches a better safety-utility frontier when initialized from the mid-trained models. Together, these results suggest that learning safety and general reasoning within a shared mid-training stage can reduce the safety-utility trade-off and make safety more robust to subsequent training.
title_ko: 안전성을 중간학습 단계에서 일반 추론과 함께 학습
tldr: 사전학습과 후학습 사이의 '안전 미드트레이닝' 단계에서 안전성과 일반 추론을 공유 구조로 함께 학습시키면, 공격 성공률이 크게 줄고 이후 SFT·RL에서도 안전성이 유지된다.
bullets: 문제: 후속 학습에서 안전성이 쉽게 사라지고, 안전 강화는 일반 성능을 해친다.
방법: 베이스 모델이 문서와 추론 과정을 스스로 생성하고 판정 모델로 걸러 중간학습에 쓴다.
결과: Qwen3 1.7B·4B·8B에서 평균 ASR이 72~81% 감소하고 일반 성능도 향상됐다.
결과: 안전 데이터 없는 SFT·GRPO 후에도 안전성이 대체로 유지됐다.
한계: 실험이 8B 이하 Qwen3·Llama3.2 모델에 한정되고 도메인·언어 범위도 제한적이다.
why: SFT 데이터에 안전 데이터가 적을 때 안전성이 무너지는 문제와, 자기생성 데이터의 형식이 안전성 유지에 미치는 영향을 다루어 실무 파인튜닝에 참고가 된다.

title: WAQS: Weight Absorption for Quadratic Probing and Affine Steering
abstract: Activation steering provides a lightweight alternative to fine-tuning for controlling large language model behavior. Existing methods, however, often face a trade-off between efficiency and expressiveness: fixed steering vectors incur negligible inference overhead but cannot adapt to the current model input, whereas input-dependent nonlinear interventions provide greater flexibility at additional runtime cost. We introduce \textbf{WAQS} (\textbf{W}eight \textbf{A}bsorption for \textbf{Q}uadratic probing and affine \textbf{S}teering), a framework that obtains state-dependent steering, without additional inference-time computation. WAQS models a concept with a quadratic probe, whose gradient yields an affine, activation-dependent steering direction. We show that this affine intervention can be folded exactly into adjacent linear transformations through an offline weight update. Moreover, we prove that quadratic functions form the maximal class of smooth concept scores whose gradient-based interventions are affine and therefore exactly absorbable into linear layers. Under a Gaussian representation model, our formulation admits an interpretation as the difference of class-conditional Mahalanobis pulls and naturally generalizes linear discriminant and difference-in-means steering. To scale to high-dimensional representations, we introduce a low-rank parameterization of the quadratic term. Across truthfulness, refusal, and sycophancy steering tasks, quadratic steering matches or improves upon constant linear steering while preserving model utility, with the absorbed implementation introducing no additional inference-time operations. Our results suggest that quadratic probes provide a practical middle ground between static linear steering and computationally expensive dynamic nonlinear interventions.
title_ko: 2차 프로브로 입력 적응형 스티어링을 가중치에 흡수
tldr: 2차(quadratic) 프로브의 기울기는 활성값에 대해 아핀(affine)이므로, 입력에 따라 달라지는 스티어링을 추론 비용 없이 가중치 업데이트로 정확히 흡수할 수 있다.
bullets: 문제: 고정 벡터 스티어링은 입력에 적응 못 하고, 비선형 방식은 추론 비용이 든다.
방법: 2차 프로브의 기울기(2Wx+w)를 인접 선형층·정규화층 가중치에 오프라인으로 접어 넣는다.
방법: 고차원 대응을 위해 2차항을 저랭크(low-rank)로 파라미터화한다.
결과: 진실성·거부·아첨 스티어링에서 고정 선형 방식과 같거나 더 낫고 유틸리티를 보존한다.
한계: 2차까지만 흡수 가능하며, 본문 일부만 확인되어 모델·수치 세부는 불명확하다.
why: 미세조정 없이 거부·아첨 같은 행동을 추론 비용 없이 교정하고 표준 체크포인트로 배포할 수 있어, 부작용 적은 행동 보정과 표현 기반 개입에 관심 있는 연구자에게 유용하다.

title: Progressive Misalignment Can Emerge from Benign Recursive Self-Distillation
abstract: Training models on their own outputs has attracted widespread attention as a possible route to advance AI capabilities. One prominent approach is self-distillation, where a model is trained to match the token-level predictions it would have produced when given access to additional context, such as a cue, feedback, or instruction. However, the safety properties of this training procedure are poorly understood. In this paper, we present a surprising safety failure of recursive self-distillation, where each self-distilled model becomes the teacher for the next round of training. We observe that when a safe model is recursively self-distilled on its own (safe) generations while receiving an additional non-harmful cue, it becomes increasingly misaligned across a diverse set of harmful queries; we call this Progressive Misalignment. We show this failure mode in both the Qwen3 and Phi-4 model families on SORRY-Bench and StrongREJECT. Progressive misalignment also occurs in a more realistic setup, where the fixed cue is replaced by feedback from a simulated user with benign intent. Using a gradient-based method, we are also able to find benign prompts that lead to progressive misalignment when applying recursive self-distillation, showing that harmful training prompts are not necessary for this failure mode to emerge. We hope our work encourages future investigations of the safety properties of AI systems recursively trained on their own data.
title_ko: 무해한 재귀 자기증류가 점진적 안전성 붕괴를 일으킴
tldr: 안전한 모델이 무해한 단서를 받으며 자기 출력으로 재귀 자기증류를 반복하면, 유해 질의에 점점 응하는 Progressive Misalignment가 나타난다.
bullets: 문제: 자기 출력 학습(자기증류)의 안전성은 거의 검증되지 않았다.
방법: 무해한 단서·피드백을 준 teacher 출력을 student가 재귀적으로 증류했다.
결과: Qwen3·Phi-4가 SORRY-Bench, StrongREJECT에서 점차 유해 요청에 응했다.
결과: 시뮬레이션 사용자 피드백과 그래디언트로 고른 무해 프롬프트에서도 발생했다.

why: 좁은 데이터로 한 학습이 넓은 행동 변화(emergent misalignment)로 번지는 사례이자, 자기증류·합성 데이터 파이프라인의 안전성과 데이터 선별 기준을 점검할 근거가 된다.

title: Compression Precedes, Content Decides: Emergent Misalignment in Reward Models
abstract: Emergent Misalignment - the out of domain generalization of narrow harmful fine-tuning first shown by Betley et al. [2025] has been widely studied in language models but not in reward models that supervise them. In this paper, we fine-tune two state-of-the-art reward models, Skywork-Reward-V2-Llama-3.1-8B and Skywork-Reward-V2-Qwen3-8B [Liu et al., 2025] and show that narrow fine-tuning reward models to prefer harm in one domain (medical or financial) generalizes to seven held out domains. This is not degeneracy, as the fine-tuned reward models lose only 4.8 and 5.3 points overall (RM-Llama) on the standard RewardBench 2 evaluation [Malik et al., 2025] while still outperforming the unmodified RM-Qwen model. We then fine-tune the underlying language models, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B using DPO [Rafailov et al., 2023] and SFT on the same data. We find that reward models are more vulnerable to preference inversions compared to their language model counterparts. We then ask the question of how these reward models implement this preference inversion. Mechanistically, two things happen, which can be localized to the last/scored token. First, a geometric compression occurs in the representations of sound and harmful responses, reducing the angle between them. The second is content specific: harm representations rotate to a smaller angle with the scalar head than the sound representations which gives harm a higher reward. This happens only in harmful preference fine-tunes and not in control.
title_ko: 보상 모델에서 나타나는 창발적 오정렬의 표현 기하 분석
tldr: 한 분야의 유해 선호 데이터 1,000쌍으로 보상 모델을 미세조정하면 다른 7개 분야에서도 선호가 뒤집히며, 이는 마지막 토큰에서 '압축'과 '내용 특이적 회전'이라는 두 단계로 구현된다.
bullets: 문제: 창발적 오정렬이 RLHF를 감독하는 보상 모델에서도 생기는지 불명확했다.
방법: Skywork 보상 모델을 의료·금융 유해 선호쌍으로 LoRA 미세조정하고 표현 각도를 분석했다.
결과: 미보유 분야에서 유해 선호가 0%에서 86~98%로 늘었고 RewardBench 2 하락은 약 5점이었다.
결과: 같은 데이터로 학습한 언어모델(SFT/DPO)보다 보상 모델의 선호 반전이 더 컸다.
한계: 압축은 무해한 공손함 대조군에서도 나타나 유해 내용만의 효과가 아니다.
why: 좁은 미세조정이 왜 넓은 행동 변화를 낳는지를 표현 기하로 풀고, 오픈 보상 모델 사용 시의 안전 위험과 대조군 설계 방식을 보여주기 때문이다.

title: MetaCurate: Evolving Curation Filters for High-Quality Agentic Coding Data
abstract: Supervised fine-tuning on agent trajectories is an effective way to improve coding agents, but selecting useful training examples requires more than identifying successful runs. A resolved patch may follow inefficient reasoning or unnecessary tool use, while a failed run may still contain useful intermediate steps. Training pipelines therefore rely on rules and qualitative assessments to filter trajectories, yet designing these filters typically requires substantial human expertise, and validating improvements through repeated training and evaluation is expensive. We introduce MetaCurate, a training-free framework that evolves executable trajectory curation filters using pairwise LLM judgments. Disagreements between the filter's rankings and the judge's preferences provide targeted feedback for jointly revising its rules, rubric, and aggregation policy. The resulting filter scores trajectories independently, so pairwise comparisons are required only during search. Starting from a blank filter, MetaCurate autonomously discovers a curation strategy that achieves competitive downstream performance without task-specific handwritten criteria. We validate downstream utility through controlled SFT experiments on our uncurated trajectory pool and the Nemotron v3 SWE dataset, with random selection and hand-authored filtering as baselines. In our experiments, MetaCurate achieves the highest mean SWE-Verified score among the compared methods, including hand-authored rule-based filtering and a training-loop baseline whose search costs 3.5x as much.
title_ko: 쌍대 비교로 코딩 에이전트 SFT 데이터 필터를 진화시키는 MetaCurate
tldr: 모델 학습 없이 LLM 심판의 쌍대 선호와 필터 순위의 불일치를 피드백 삼아 궤적 선별 필터(규칙·루브릭·집계 정책)를 스스로 개선하는 프레임워크이다.
bullets: 문제: 성공 여부만으로는 에이전트 궤적의 SFT 가치를 알 수 없고 수작업 필터는 비싸다.
방법: 심판과 필터의 쌍 순위 불일치로 규칙·루브릭·정책을 함께 수정한다.
방법: 완성된 필터는 궤적을 개별 채점해 쌍 비교는 탐색 때만 쓴다.

title: Exploring The Empirical Privacy Landscape of Synthetic Data
abstract: Methods for training language models on sensitive data differ in how they balance capability gains against the risk of leaking private information. In this paper, we present a controlled comparison of data-level and training-level interventions for navigating the capability-privacy tradeoff on synthetic medical records with canaries to probe for leakage. Direct finetuning performs best on capability metrics but leads to the most privacy leakage, while DP-SGD reduces leakage at substantial cost to capabilities. Generating synthetic data from these records offers a more favorable balance, particularly when guided by a uniqueness-aware instruction to replace private details. Relative to naive paraphrasing, privacy-aware rewriting improves privacy protection across a variety of different rewriting models. We also find that more capable rewriting models generally reduce the risks of downstream privacy leakage, although held-out fit does not improve monotonically and increased test-time compute yields inconsistent gains. Overall, these results highlight privacy-aware rewriting as a promising direction for achieving a more favorable trade-off between capabilities and empirical privacy compared to other training-level methods, and our evaluation framework supports comparisons of future models and methods.

title: Risk and Refusal: Mechanisms of LLM Responses to Suicidal Ideation
abstract: Refusal is a common safety mechanism in large language models (LLMs), yet in contexts of suicidal ideation (SI), refusing to engage can itself constitute a safety failure. We evaluate how eight instruction-tuned LLMs respond to SI and self-harm disclosures across three datasets, varying whether models are informed that a disclosure expresses SI and whether they receive a clinician-developed response protocol, and complement this with mechanistic analyses in six open-weight models. Our results reveal a nuanced relationship between refusal and response-level risk. At baseline, elevated risk in model responses is driven primarily by inattention to the disclosure, alongside refusal to engage. Mechanistic analyses suggest that models may refuse SI disclosures through the same direction that mediates their refusals of harmful requests. However, informing models of the SI context, or suppressing refusal directly, increases engagement without reliably lowering response risk, and may raise it. In contrast, the clinician-guided protocol consistently reduces response-level risk while also reducing refusal. Together, these analyses and ablations motivate the need for models that refuse only when warranted and engage in interactionally safe ways when users disclose SI.

title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning
abstract: Language model agents increasingly automate post-training, but when given the full training stack they converge on supervised fine-tuning and spend most effort revising training data. Existing systems give the agent one kind of control, selecting rows from a fixed pool or calling a generator, whereas a human data engineer adjusts proportions, prunes, repairs, replaces and synthesizes the data. We design a data action space for these changes and ask whether an automated system can make the full range rather than one of them, and what structure that requires. We first run this loop with a single agent, and it reaches only one action, adjusting category proportions, while its context fills with execution output and is discarded mid-search. We therefore introduce AutoSFT, a multi-agent system where a meta agent separates execution from analysis, gathers proposals from independent angles, and calls a synthesis subagent for capabilities the pool cannot cover, with the model, the trainer, and the budget fixed within each comparison. Adding each component in turn helps: the executor halves context loss, the analysis subagents lift the best IFEval by +6.5, and synthesis adds +3.4 IFEval and +2.9 IFBench. The same loop transfers to code, where analysis adds +3.7 MBPP+ over a single agent that does not improve. Every result comes from runs that retrain from the base model each round, so each component's effect is individually attributable. Our findings suggest that automating SFT data research depends more on covering diverse data actions than on a stronger single action.

title: Behavioral Compositionality of Sparse Autoencoder Representations
comment: 29 pages, 9 figures. Code: this https URL
abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) represent model activations with sparse, linearly decoded features, but the downstream effects of those features need not compose additively. We introduce SAE Additivity Residuals (SAR), which measure the behavioral variation left unexplained above a chosen interaction order. Under independent feature subset sampling, population SAR is exactly the normalized energy of interactions above that order and bounds coalition ordering error for the optimal low order approximation. To distinguish compositionality associated with the SAE representation from that induced by downstream computation, we compare learned SAE coordinates with sum preserving random rotations of the same selected subspace and find lower first order residuals for the learned coordinates across all 18 model and behavior settings. The coordinates are nevertheless not fully additive: pairwise terms improve held out coalition ordering in every setting and outperform parameter matched models using randomly selected third order terms. In a combined steering experiment, pairwise modeling raises rank fidelity from 0.5874 to 0.7790 and reduces ordering error from 0.1444 to 0.0606. Together, these results show that SAE coordinates support comparatively compositional behavioral descriptions while faithful joint explanations and interventions still require interactions beyond individual feature effects. Code is available at https://github.com/OpenSAE/SAE-Behavioral-Compositionality.
title_ko: SAE 특징들의 합산 가능성과 상호작용 측정

title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
abstract: Context can improve large language model performance, but these gains may be lost after context removal. Inspired by biological systems consolidation, we formulate Memory Consolidation (MC) as internalizing these gains while preserving non-target capabilities, connecting context-specified editing, skill learning, and behavioral steering under a common objective. We introduce a five-task-family testbed measuring consolidation and retention under single, batch, and sequential updates. We propose Cortex, which generates prospective queries to anticipate uses of context and distills context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural feed-forward network updates. Across 4B--120B dense and mixture-of-experts backbones, including both text-only and multimodal models, Cortex lies on the empirical consolidation--retention Pareto frontier in most evaluated settings. After 50 sequential factual edits on a 14B model, Cortex-Structural recovers 88.9% of the context-induced gain while retaining 99.8% of original non-target performance.
title_ko: 컨텍스트를 모델 파라미터 메모리로 내재화하는 Cortex
tldr: 프롬프트 컨텍스트의 효과를 저랭크/FFN 업데이트로 증류해 컨텍스트 없이도 유지하면서 기존 능력은 보존하는 방법을 제안한다.

title: Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation
abstract: Continual post-training faces a dual challenge of acquisition and retention: models must learn new capabilities while preserving prior knowledge. While Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) mitigates this using self-supervision with in-context demonstrations, it relies on strong in-context learning and instruction-following abilities. Consequently, SDFT fails on smaller models critical for low-latency, on-device use. To enable continual learning at smaller scales, we first identify the root cause of failure. We show that poor acquisition and forgetting correlate linearly with the post-trained model's distribution shift, revealing the necessity of in-distribution learning. We thus introduce Synthetic Self-Distillation (SynthSelf), imitating SDFT's in-distribution rewrite by outsourcing the task to a minimally larger, same-family aligner. Coupled with off-policy supervision and rejection sampling, this provides the high-quality supervision small models require without breaking their original distribution. Evaluations spanning 4 acquisition datasets (including a mixture) and 14 retention benchmarks show SynthSelf consistently outperforms 6 methods (including off- and on-policy distillation) across 3 small model scales. Extensive further analyses confirm SynthSelf paves the way toward effective small-model continual learning.
title_ko: 소형 모델의 지속 학습을 위한 합성 자기증류 SynthSelf

title: The Thinking Leakage in Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
abstract: Hybrid reasoning models such as the Qwen3 series switch between a THINK mode and a NO-THINK mode through a few chat-template tokens. A popular recipe trains such models with reinforcement learning in NO-THINK mode and reports improved reasoning performance. We provide evidence that much of this gain can be explained by thinking leakage: the gain comes largely from partially reactivating the reasoning abilities of the original model's THINK mode instead of learning enhanced reasoning behavior. We train Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B with GRPO in NO-THINK mode. As accuracy improves, responses become longer and more reflective, are increasingly judged by the original model to resemble its own thinking, and the model's internal activations shift toward its THINK mode. We then investigate at the level of weights, activations, and attention heads: scaling the RL update further elicits THINK-mode behavior and approaches THINK-mode accuracy but does not exceed it; in Qwen3-8B, replacing a low-dimensional THINK-related activation subspace of the RL-trained model with its original-model value removes most of the RL gain, and the reverse exchange transfers a considerable fraction of the gain to the original model; and the RL-induced shift passes through the attention heads that read the empty think block. We further identify a possible mechanism in the GRPO training signal: responses favored by the advantage-weighted update are more THINK-like, and a gradient step computed from this signal moves the model toward its THINK state. Thus, gains in NO-THINK mode can largely reflect reactivation of reasoning abilities already present in the original model.
title_ko: Qwen3 NO-THINK RL 성능 향상은 THINK 모드 재활성화

abstract: Westernizing Qwen: Measuring and Mitigating Geopolitical Alignment in Chinese Open-Weight LLMs Solutions For AI & Product Teams For Security & Privacy Teams For Frontier AI Labs Data QA Blog About Book a demo Book a demo Behavior Unlearning // Westernizing Westernizing Qwen: Measuring and Mitigating Geopolitical Alignment in Chinese Open-Weight LLMs By Ilana Grinberg October 5, 2026 TL;DR: Chinese open-weight models are becoming default building blocks for Western enterprises, and they carry the Chinese Communist Party's political alignment in their weights. To address it, we introduce Westernized LLMs: applying Hirundo’s unlearning technology to realign Chinese LLMs to Western standards, by directly editing their weights. On the base Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 89.8% of responses showed CCP-aligned censorship, propaganda or bias. After Unlearning, our Westernized Qwen cut that rate to 2.8%, while preserving performance across coding, reasoning and science tasks. In parallel, we are also soon releasing a new benchmark, covering CCP-alignment in LLMs. ‍ THE PROBLEM: POLITICAL ALIGNMENT SHIPS INSIDE THE WEIGHTS Chinese labs have gone from a rounding error to a leading share of open-model usage
title_ko: Qwen의 친중 정치 정렬을 언러닝으로 제거하고 측정
tldr: Hirundo는 Qwen3.6의 CCP 정렬 행동을 LoRA 기반 행동 언러닝으로 89.8%에서 2.8%까지 낮췄고, 일반 성능과 안전성은 거의 유지했다고 주장한다.
bullets: 문제: 중국 오픈웨이트 모델은 검열·선전 편향이 가중치에 내재되어 있다.
방법: 편향 응답을 골라 LoRA로 언러닝하고, retain set으로 나머지를 고정 후 병합.
결과: CCPC-500 89.8%→2.8%, 코딩·추론 벤치 하락은 최대 1.83%p.
한계: 벤더 블로그라 자체 벤치마크·판정 기준이며 아직 공개 전, 독립 검증이 없다.
why: 좁은 행동(정치 검열)만 부작용 없이 가중치에서 지우는 언러닝 접근과 과거절·안전성 보존 평가 방식을 실제 사례로 볼 수 있다.

title: Visual Grounding Safety in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly trained to generate structured outputs like points and bounding boxes that downstream interfaces, agents, and robots can act on, yet safety alignment of this output channel has not been systematically analyzed. We study visual grounding safety by repurposing three safety benchmarks spanning direct harm (VLSU), social bias (BBQ-V), and situational safety (Asimov-2.0) into 15,401 matched pairs of harmful requests that differ only in the requested output: a free-text answer (VQA) or a grounding (point or bounding box). Across five VLMs, models that refuse a harmful request posed as a question often comply when the same request asks for a grounding: averaged over models, grounding refusal trails VQA refusal by 31-59 percentage points, depending on the domain, and safety system prompts do not close this gap. We propose a fine-tuning approach that combines grounding-form refusals with capability grounding data and self-distilled benign data to counter over-refusal. For Qwen3-VL-8B and VisionReasoner-7B, it improves grounding refusal by 77-95 percentage points on VLSU and BBQ-V and by 64-85 points on the held-out Asimov-2.0 domain, while also improving VQA refusal, preserving grounding capability, and keeping over-refusal limited. Representation analysis shows that fine-tuning moves harmful requests toward each model's refusal direction, most strongly for grounding, while leaving benign requests near the harmless reference.
title_ko: VLM 시각 그라운딩 출력의 안전성 격차 분석과 보정
tldr: 질문에는 유해 요청을 거절하는 VLM도 같은 요청이 점·박스 좌표 출력 형태면 쉽게 따르며, 그라운딩 형태 거절 데이터와 자기증류 정상 데이터로 파인튜닝하면 이 격차를 크게 줄일 수 있다.
bullets: 문제: VLM은 유해 요청을 VQA로는 거절해도 좌표 출력으로는 따른다.
방법: 15,401쌍의 VQA/그라운딩 짝 평가셋을 만들어 5개 VLM을 비교했다.
결과: 그라운딩 거절률이 VQA보다 평균 31~59%p 낮았고 시스템 프롬프트로도 안 메워졌다.
방법: 그라운딩형 거절, 능력 데이터, 자기증류 정상 데이터를 섞어 파인튜닝했다.
한계: 실험이 Qwen3-VL-8B와 VisionReasoner-7B 두 모델에 한정되고 코드는 미공개다.
why: 출력 형식이 바뀌면 안전 정렬이 일반화되지 않는 문제와, 자기증류 정상 데이터로 과거절을 막는 데이터 구성, 거절 방향 표현 분석을 함께 다뤄 안전 파인튜닝 설계에 참고가 된다.

title: Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data
comment: Project page: this https URL Code: this https URL
abstract: In this paper, we study how training data creates associations between the tokens at the start of a base model's response and the reasoning behavior that follows. First, we demonstrate that fixing particular starting token cues makes a base model's performance competitive with that of its reinforcement learning (RL)-trained counterparts on math and coding. For instance, the cue ".\n\nOkay" raises Olmo-3-7B's MATH-500 pass@1 accuracy from 42% to 78%, while "Alright," raises Qwen3-14B's from 72% to 87%. Second, RL makes these cues more likely, while fixing them recovers much of its performance gain over the base model. Third, we trace the reasoning effects of token cues to the training data. We perform causal data interventions to turn an arbitrary word, such as "chicken", into an effective reasoning cue, or remove an existing cue's effect. A similar edit makes the prompt instruction "Think duck duck goose" as effective as "Think step by step" at eliciting reasoning. We also find that the hidden state representations induced by different cues correlate with different document types from the training set. Finally, we extend our study of token cues with a case study in language model safety, finding that different cues elicit distinct refusal and compliance behaviors that correspond to different types of training data.
title_ko: 베이스 모델의 시작 토큰 단서가 학습 데이터 연상으로 추론을 이끌어냄
tldr: 베이스 모델 응답의 첫 두 토큰(예: '.\n\nOkay')만 고정해도 RL 모델에 필적하는 추론 성능이 나오며, 이 단서의 효과는 학습 데이터의 연상에서 비롯됨을 데이터 반사실 실험으로 보였다.
bullets: 문제: RL이 새 추론 능력을 가르치는지, 기존 능력을 끌어내는지 불분명하다.
방법: 시작 토큰 단서를 고정하고, 사전학습 데이터의 단어를 치환해 재학습했다.
결과: Olmo-3-7B의 MATH-500이 단서로 42%에서 78%, RL 모델은 75%였다.
결과: 'okay'를 'chicken'으로 바꾸자 해당 단서 정확도가 2.4%에서 37.2%로 올랐다.
한계: R1-Zero식 RL만 다뤘고 Llama-3.1-8B에는 효과적인 단서가 없었다.
why: 좁은 데이터 편집이 모델 행동을 크게 바꾼다는 점과, 단서별 은닉 상태가 학습 문서 유형과 대응하고 거부/순응 행동도 달라진다는 점이 데이터 큐레이션·안전성 관점에서 참고할 만하다.
